findings.reason: a node would set its per-batch ceiling from a near-empty batch and call its witness met by another plan's write, so both instruments would report a pass on work this section did not do.
findings.text: the spend paragraph is unchanged while the section's trigger changed: "batch 1 measures the real per-name cost and every later batch runs under a ceiling" still points at batch-001, which sib-consistency-batches.json records as the flux-surface-average concept group, and sn-definitions-by-construction §6's done-when reports bringing the flux-surface average from 8 forms to one before §2 starts — so the rate the whole spend control rests on would be measured on a batch that has nothing left to do, and §2's named witness ("the flux-surface-average family reads with one definition and one documentation template", line 50) restates what §6 already delivers rather than witnessing §2's residual work
